title: Glendale
name: Glendale
metaDescription: 1031 exchange coordination for Glendale corporate office towers, Brand Boulevard retail centers, and rent-stabilized multifamily near Los Angeles.

sections.html: Glendale pairs a corporate office base with two large retail centers and a residential population that has kept its apartment market steady even when other Los Angeles submarkets have cooled. An exchange buyer here typically weighs office towers along Brand Boulevard against the retail draw of Americana at Brand and the Glendale Galleria, with a quieter multifamily market sitting underneath both.

sections.heading: Brand Boulevard's Corporate Office Corridor
sections.html:
Glendale's downtown office towers along Brand Boulevard have long attracted corporate headquarters and back-office tenants looking for lower rents than Downtown Los Angeles or Century City without giving up freeway access or a walkable downtown. A replacement buyer should confirm how much of a specific building's rent roll depends on a single anchor corporate tenant, since Glendale's office market has fewer large tenants overall than downtown or the Westside.

Because several of these towers were built for a single large occupant and later subdivided as that tenant's space needs changed, floor plates and elevator-bank configurations can be less efficient for a true multi-tenant leasing strategy than a building designed from the start for a diversified roster. A buyer planning to re-lease vacant floors to smaller tenants should walk the specific floor plate rather than assume it re-subdivides as easily as a newer, purpose-built multi-tenant tower.

sections.heading: Two Retail Centers, Two Different Draws
sections.html:
Americana at Brand functions as an open-air lifestyle center centered on dining and entertainment tenants, while the adjacent Glendale Galleria runs a more traditional enclosed-mall tenant mix. The two centers pull from overlapping trade areas but attract different retailers, and a retail replacement buyer should treat them as competing rather than complementary properties when reviewing nearby comparable sales.

A retail parcel positioned between the two centers should be underwritten on its own merits rather than assumed to capture spillover foot traffic from either, since shoppers visiting Americana at Brand and shoppers visiting the Galleria do not always cross between the two at the rate a casual site visit might suggest. Confirming actual anchor-tenant sales performance nearby, where a seller will share it, tells a buyer more than proximity alone.

sections.heading: A Steadier Multifamily Base
sections.html:
Glendale's apartment market, much of it serving a long-established Armenian-American community alongside newer residents commuting to Burbank and downtown Los Angeles, has generally held occupancy more steadily than some coastal or entertainment-district submarkets. Rent stabilization coverage still applies to a meaningful share of older buildings here, so a multifamily replacement buyer should confirm construction date and coverage status the same way they would in Los Angeles proper rather than assuming Glendale's separate municipal boundary changes that analysis.

Multigenerational households are more common in this rental base than in some younger, more transient Los Angeles submarkets, and that pattern tends to show up as longer average tenancy and lower unit turnover on a rent roll. A buyer should weigh that lower turnover against the corresponding limit on how quickly rents can reset to market on a stabilized unit, since the two effects work in opposite directions on projected income growth.

sections.heading: The Glendale Identification Set
sections.html:
A typical Glendale list includes:

  • Brand Boulevard corporate and back-office towers
  • retail space in or adjacent to Americana at Brand and Glendale Galleria
  • rent-stabilized apartment buildings in the older residential neighborhoods
  • newer mid-rise multifamily near downtown Glendale

sections.heading: Why Glendale Often Backs Up a Burbank or Downtown List
sections.html: Because Glendale sits between Burbank's studio-driven market and Downtown Los Angeles' larger office base, it functions well as a backup identification for buyers targeting either, offering comparable freeway access at generally lower office pricing. A qualified intermediary coordinating a Glendale closing should confirm the lender is comfortable underwriting a corporate-anchor office building with a thinner overall tenant roster than a downtown tower would carry.

faqs.q: What kind of tenants occupy Brand Boulevard office buildings?
faqs.a: Corporate headquarters and back-office tenants make up a large share of the market, drawn by lower rents than downtown or Century City while keeping freeway access and a walkable downtown, though a handful of buildings do carry a more diversified professional-services tenant roster.

faqs.q: How do Americana at Brand and Glendale Galleria compare as retail investments?
faqs.a: They pull from overlapping trade areas but run different tenant mixes, an open-air lifestyle format versus a traditional enclosed mall, so a buyer should treat them as competing centers rather than assuming shared performance trends, and should pull anchor-tenant sales data specific to whichever center a target parcel actually sits near.

faqs.q: Does rent stabilization apply to Glendale apartment buildings?
faqs.a: It applies to a meaningful share of older buildings in the city, similar to how it works in Los Angeles proper, so a buyer should confirm a specific building's construction date and coverage status rather than assume Glendale's separate municipal boundary changes the analysis.

faqs.q: Why would a buyer pair a Glendale identification with a Burbank property?
faqs.a: Glendale sits between Burbank's studio-driven office market and downtown Los Angeles' larger base, so it offers comparable freeway access at generally lower pricing, making it a practical backup on a three-property list if entitlement or lender timing on the primary candidate slips.

faqs.q: Is Glendale office space concentrated among a few large tenants?
faqs.a: Often, yes, so a buyer should confirm how much of a specific building's rent roll depends on one anchor corporate tenant before assuming a diversified, low-risk rent roll, and should ask how the building's floor plates would subdivide if that tenant did not renew.
